metadata.case_name: LAU HO MING v. WONG PAK HO

source: the Plaintiff was found to have "visual acuity of right eye 6/15, left eye 6/7/5, right full thickness corneal laceration, right ciliary spasm and commotion retinae [ie retinal oedema] at superior retina. Repair of right ruptured eyeball and examination under anaesthesia was performed …… [and] the corneal wound healed uneventfully. ……"

injuries.description: L-shaped corneal scars with surrounding corneal opacities and induced irregular astigmatism (right eye)
source: the corneal lacerations of the Plaintiff’s right eye resolved with the formation of L-shaped corneal scars with surrounding corneal opacities in his right eye. Such lacerations reduce his right eye vision because of corneal opacities, corneal scars and induced irregular astigmatism.
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration without prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

manifestations.description: intermittent grittiness of his right eye
mild right eye photophobia (undue sensitivity of an eye to light)
has to rely mainly on his left eye for visual tasks
impairment of his near vision (has to stop reading after 5 minutes or so)
has to remove spectacles every 15 minutes because of eye discomfort
redness of right eye upon wearing contact lens
dizziness and pain in right eye after reading for over 5 minutes
difficulty making out bus route numbers and often misses the bus or gets on the wrong bus
left eye tires easily when used for visual tasks

treatments_received: urgent referral to Eye Clinic of Caritas Medical Centre
repair of right ruptured eyeball and examination under anaesthesia
removal of corneal stitches (operation on cornea)
follow up appointments at Eye Clinic (frequent and monthly thereafter)

losses.description: Impairment of right visual acuity due to corneal scars, opacities and induced irregular astigmatism causing reduced right eye vision and reliance on left eye

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Has to rely on left eye to aim cue stick when playing snooker and to identify chess or mahjong pieces; left eye tires easily affecting leisure and entertainment habits
Goes out less than before as a result of impaired right visual acuity

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy quiet or solitude
losses.description: Difficulty reading newspapers (has to stop after about 5 minutes due to dizziness and pain in right eye)

comparable_cases.case_name: Sze Ping Chui v Lau Ching Wai
comparable_cases.injury_description: Ruptured left eyeball with a 5mm full thickness linear corneal laceration at the visual axis and cataract, and the lens was also damaged. Urgent operation done for repair of the cornea with removal of the damaged lens and implantation of intra-ocular lens; best-corrected visual acuity 0.3 and 6/18; resulting permanent disability and photophobia leading to award of HK$400,000.00 for PSLA.
